questions.text: Cellulose nitrate film fires cannot be extinguished by smothering (CO₂ or inert gas systems). What fundamental chemical property of cellulose nitrate makes conventional gas-based suppression ineffective?

options.text: Self-oxidizing — the film contains its own chemically bound oxygen and continues burning without external air supply
High surface-area-to-mass ratio — the film burns too quickly for smothering agents to take effect before combustion completes
Thermoplastic behavior — the film melts and flows, spreading fire even after surface oxygen is depleted by suppression
Catalytic decomposition — heat from suppression agents accelerates rather than suppresses combustion through exothermic reaction

questions.rationale: Original question was already source-correct and substantive; the prior edit (source-audited-article-batch-048) was degenerate, with 1-character garbage in 3 of 4 option text fields and a nonsensical rationale. Restored the original verbatim. Original source rationale: Cellulose nitrate contains oxygen chemically bound within the nitrate ester groups of its polymer chain. This means it burns vigorously even in an oxygen-depleted atmosphere and cannot be extinguished by CO₂, Halon, or any smothering agent. Water or water solutions are the specified first aid agents because they absorb heat and reduce spread rate — the only effective approach against a self-oxidizing fire. The 1929 Cleveland Clinic disaster (123 deaths from toxic gas inhalation) was the historical catalyst for international film storage standards.

questions.text: A six-storey building installs a dry standpipe with a 100mm diameter riser. How many inlets must the Siamese connection provide at street level?

options.text: One 100mm inlet, matching the riser diameter
Two inlets, as required for a 100mm standpipe
Three inlets, as required for a 100mm standpipe
Four inlets, as required for a 100mm standpipe

questions.rationale: Original question was already source-correct and substantive; the prior edit (source-audited-article-batch-048) was degenerate, with 1-character garbage in 3 of 4 option text fields and a nonsensical rationale. Restored the original verbatim. Original source rationale: Sec. 1212 specifies Siamese connection inlet count by riser diameter: 100mm standpipe requires a 2-way Siamese, 125mm requires 3-way, and 150mm requires 4-way.
questions.explanation: The inlet count scales with standpipe diameter because larger risers demand more simultaneous water supply from fire department pumper trucks. A 100mm riser at 900 L/min can be fed by two 63mm fire hose connections, making the 2-way Siamese the correct choice.

questions.text: At what maximum height above the finished floor must a dry standpipe hose outlet valve be installed to remain within firefighter reach?

options.text: 900 millimeters above the finished floor level
1,050 millimeters above the finished floor level
1,200 millimeters above the finished floor level
1,500 millimeters above the finished floor level

questions.rationale: Original question was already source-correct and substantive; the prior edit (source-audited-article-batch-048) was degenerate, with 1-character garbage in 3 of 4 option text fields and a nonsensical rationale. Restored the original verbatim. Original source rationale: Sec. 1212 specifies that dry standpipe hose outlet valves must be located no higher than 1.20m above the floor to ensure firefighters in full gear can operate them quickly under stress.
questions.explanation: The 1.20m maximum height accounts for ergonomic reach while wearing firefighting equipment and gloves. Valves installed too high create dangerous delays during emergency response. The same 300mm to 1.20m range applies to Siamese connection heights above exterior grade.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Sec. 1212, what is the minimum floor area threshold that triggers automatic sprinkler requirements for habitation occupancies?

options.text: 150 square meters of gross floor area per storey
200 square meters of gross floor area per storey
250 square meters of gross floor area per storey
300 square meters of gross floor area per storey

questions.rationale: Original question was already source-correct and substantive; the prior edit (source-audited-article-batch-048) was degenerate, with 1-character garbage in 3 of 4 option text fields and a nonsensical rationale. Restored the original verbatim. Original source rationale: Sec. 1212 specifies a dual trigger: floor area must be 200 sq.m or more AND occupant load must exceed 20 persons. Both conditions must be met for habitation occupancies.
questions.explanation: The 200 sq.m threshold is only half the trigger. The occupant load condition (>20 persons for habitation, >10 for workshops) must also be satisfied. A 250 sq.m space with only 5 occupants would not trigger the sprinkler requirement.

questions.text: A building's fire pump must deliver a minimum flow of 1,000 liters per minute. A gravity tank is also being considered as the sole water supply. What is the critical minimum tank capacity requirement that would allow the gravity tank to replace the fire pump?

options.text: The gravity tank must hold at least 9,000 liters to supply 10 minutes at pump flow
The gravity tank must supply 1,500 liters per minute for a minimum of 10 minutes
The gravity tank must hold at least 15,000 liters and maintain 2.0 kg/sq.cm at the outlet
The gravity tank must supply 1,000 liters per minute for a minimum of 30 minutes

questions.rationale: Original question was already source-correct and substantive; the prior edit (source-audited-article-batch-048) was degenerate, with 1-character garbage in 3 of 4 option text fields and a nonsensical rationale. Restored the original verbatim. Original source rationale: Sec. 1212 specifies that when a gravity tank serves as the water supply, it must be capable of delivering 1,500 L/min for not less than 10 minutes. This is a higher flow rate than the fire pump minimum (1,000 L/min) to account for gravity supply pressure limitations.
questions.explanation: The gravity tank's 1,500 L/min threshold is 50% higher than the fire pump's 1,000 L/min minimum because gravity tanks lack the pressure consistency of active pumps. The 10-minute minimum duration ensures at least initial fire suppression while the fire department responds. A tank sized only for the pump flow rate (1,000 L/min × 10 min = 10,000 L) would be non-compliant; the tank must be sized for 15,000 L minimum.

questions.text: An assembly hall with 600 occupants has its dispersal area located 20 meters from the nearest exit. Does this hall require an automatic sprinkler system under PD 1096?

options.text: No, because the dispersal area is less than 30 meters from the exit
Yes, because the occupant load alone exceeds 500 persons
Yes, because both conditions — over 500 occupants and exits over 30 meters from dispersal — must be evaluated independently
No, because assembly halls are exempt from sprinkler requirements under Sec. 1212

questions.rationale: Original question was already source-correct and substantive; the prior edit (source-audited-article-batch-048) was degenerate, with 1-character garbage in 3 of 4 option text fields and a nonsensical rationale. Restored the original verbatim. Original source rationale: Assembly halls trigger the sprinkler requirement only when BOTH conditions are met: occupant load exceeds 500 AND exits are more than 30m from the dispersal area. With exits only 20m away, the second condition is not satisfied even though the occupant load exceeds 500.
questions.explanation: This is a conjunction (AND) condition, not a disjunction (OR). The occupant load threshold alone is insufficient — the physical distance from the dispersal area to the exit must also exceed 30m. When exits are close to the dispersal area, rapid occupant egress makes the sprinkler requirement unnecessary for assembly halls specifically.

questions.text: A roof-level fire standpipe outlet must be fitted with what configuration to allow simultaneous connection of fire department equipment?

options.text: A single 63mm gate valve outlet with a pressure gauge
A 2-way 63mm Siamese connection with two gate valves
A single 100mm butterfly valve outlet at roof parapet level
A 3-way 50mm hose connection with individual shut-off valves

questions.rationale: Original question was already source-correct and substantive; the prior edit (source-audited-article-batch-048) was degenerate, with 1-character garbage in 3 of 4 option text fields and a nonsensical rationale. Restored the original verbatim. Original source rationale: Sec. 1212 requires the roof termination of a dry standpipe to have a 2-way Siamese connection with 63mm outlets, enabling helicopter-assisted fire-fighting operations and rooftop cooling water supply.
questions.explanation: The 2-way 63mm roof outlet matches the diameter specified for hose connections throughout the dry standpipe system. The dual-outlet Siamese configuration allows two hose lines to be deployed from the roof simultaneously, which is essential for top-down fire attack on upper floors.

questions.text: Which building condition independently triggers the requirement for a dry standpipe system under PD 1096?

options.text: A building whose footprint exceeds 500 square meters on any single floor
A building with four or more storeys above grade
A building with basement parking of more than two levels
A building whose total gross floor area exceeds 1,000 square meters

questions.rationale: Original question was already source-correct and substantive; the prior edit (source-audited-article-batch-048) was degenerate, with 1-character garbage in 3 of 4 option text fields and a nonsensical rationale. Restored the original verbatim. Original source rationale: Under Sec. 1212, a dry standpipe system is required in any building four storeys or more in height, regardless of floor area or occupancy load.
questions.explanation: The four-storey threshold is height-based and stands alone as a trigger. A four-storey 400 sq.m building with few occupants still requires a dry standpipe because manual hose access to upper floors from ground-level fire trucks becomes impractical.

questions.text: A dry standpipe system must be hydrostatically tested to what pressure before being placed in service?

options.text: 10 kilograms per square centimeter for 30 minutes
15 kilograms per square centimeter for 15 minutes
20 kilograms per square centimeter for the required duration
25 kilograms per square centimeter for the required duration

questions.rationale: Original question was already source-correct and substantive; the prior edit (source-audited-article-batch-048) was degenerate, with 1-character garbage in 3 of 4 option text fields and a nonsensical rationale. Restored the original verbatim. Original source rationale: Sec. 1212 requires dry standpipe systems to be hydrostatically tested at 20 kg/sq.cm before being declared serviceable for fire-fighting operations.
questions.explanation: The 20 kg/sq.cm test pressure is significantly higher than normal operating pressure to ensure the system can withstand surge pressures from fire pump activation. Failure at this test pressure indicates defective pipe joints or fittings.

questions.text: A building is provided with an automatic sprinkler system throughout. By how much does this extend the allowable travel distance to the nearest exit compared to a non-sprinklered building?

options.text: The travel distance increases from 30 meters to 45 meters
The travel distance increases from 45 meters to 60 meters
The travel distance increases from 60 meters to 75 meters
The travel distance increases from 45 meters to 90 meters

questions.rationale: Original question was already source-correct and substantive; the prior edit (source-audited-article-batch-048) was degenerate, with 1-character garbage in 3 of 4 option text fields and a nonsensical rationale. Restored the original verbatim. Original source rationale: Under Sec. 1207 read together with Sec. 1212, the allowable travel distance without sprinklers is 45m. Full sprinkler coverage extends this to 60m, a 33% increase reflecting the additional evacuation time sprinklers provide.
questions.explanation: Sprinklers allow the 45m→60m travel distance extension because they suppress or control a fire, buying occupants additional safe evacuation time. This trade-off is frequently used in large open-plan offices or shopping centers where placing exits at 45m intervals would be architecturally disruptive.
questions.code_citation: PD 1096, Rule XII, Sec. 1207 and Sec. 1212

questions.text: A wet standpipe system's hose outlet must deliver water at what minimum flow rate and pressure combination at the most hydraulically disadvantaged outlet?

options.text: 150 liters per minute at 1.5 kilograms per square centimeter minimum pressure
190 liters per minute at 2.0 kilograms per square centimeter minimum pressure
250 liters per minute at 2.5 kilograms per square centimeter minimum pressure
300 liters per minute at 3.0 kilograms per square centimeter minimum pressure

questions.rationale: Original question was already source-correct and substantive; the prior edit (source-audited-article-batch-048) was degenerate, with 1-character garbage in 3 of 4 option text fields and a nonsensical rationale. Restored the original verbatim. Original source rationale: Sec. 1212 establishes the wet standpipe performance standard as 190 L/min at a minimum residual pressure of 2.0 kg/sq.cm at the hydraulically most disadvantaged outlet.
questions.explanation: The 190 L/min at 2.0 kg/sq.cm represents the minimum acceptable fire-fighting flow at the worst-case outlet (typically the highest floor, farthest from the pump). Systems must be designed to exceed this at all other outlets when this condition is met.
